source_text: τίας ἧς ἥμαρτε, θῆλυ ἀπὸ τῶν προβάτων, ἀμνάδα ἢ χίμαιραν ἐξ αἰγῶν περὶ ἁμαρτίας, καὶ ἐξιλάσεται περὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ ἱερεὺς περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ, ἧς ἥμαρτε, καὶ ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ ἡ ἁμαρτία.» Ἄθρει δὴ οὖν ὅτι τὸν ὁρκισμοῦ φωνῆς ἐπαΐοντα, καὶ παρ' οὐδὲν ὅλως τὸ πρᾶγμα πεποιημένον, καὶ τὸν ἑτέροις ἔνοχον μολυσμοῖς, καὶ μὴν ἐπὶ τούτῳ, τὸν ἐπὶ τῇ ψευδορκίᾳ κατεγνωσμένον, ἐν ἴσῳ τε καὶ ἀπαραλλάκτῳ τίθησι πλημμελείας τρόπῳ· μολυσμὸς γὰρ ἀληθῶς ἐξαίσιος, καὶ εἰς αὐτό που τὸ λοῖσθον ἀναθρώσκει τῶν κακῶν, ἡ εἰς Θεὸν καταφρόνησις, καὶ ταῖς σαρκικαῖς ἀκαθαρσίαις ἐγγύς τε καὶ ἀδελφὸν τὸ πλημμέλημα, ἢ οὐκ ἐν ἴσῳ θετέον λόγῳ τὴν ἐπάρατον ψευδορκίαν καὶ ὁρκισμοῦ καταφρόνησιν; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν· ἰσοπαλῆ γάρ πως ἐπ' ἀμφοῖν ἀεὶ τὰ ἐγκλήματα. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἕψεται δὴ οὖν καὶ τούτοις ἡ λύσις δι' ἐξαγορεύσεώς τε καὶ μὴν καὶ ἀμνάδος, ἤτοι προβάτου σφαγῆς· «Λέγε γὰρ σὺ τὰς ἀνομίας σου πρῶτος,» φησὶν, «ἵνα δικαιωθῇς.» Καὶ μὴν καὶ ὁ θεῖος ἀναφωνεῖ Δαβίδ· «Εἶπα· Ἐξαγορεύσω κατ' ἐμοῦ τὴν ἀνομίαν μου τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ σὺ ἀφῆκας τὴν ἀσέβειαν τῆς καρδίας μου.» Πλὴν, οὐκ ἀπόχρη εἰς τὴν τελείαν ἀπόνιψιν τὸ ἐξαγορεῦσαι μόνον, ἀπαλλάττει δὲ παντελῶς ὁ Χριστοῦ θάνατος, παθόντος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, καὶ ταῖς ἁπάντων ἡμῶν ἁμαρτίαις ἑαυτὸν ὑποφέροντος ὡς ἐν εἴδει παντὶ τῶν ἡμέρων ζώων· ἐν μόσχῳ δὴ λέγω, καὶ μὴν καὶ προβάτῳ καὶ αἰγί. Ἀπροφάσιστον δὲ ὥσπερ καθιστὰς ὁ νόμος τὸ ῥᾴθυμον εἰς θυσίαν, τοῖς ἐν μολυσμοῖς καὶ ἀκαθαρσίαις, εἰ μὴ μόσχον τις ἔχοι καὶ πρόβατον, τοῖς κατὰ χεῖρα καὶ ἐν ἰσχύϊ τιμᾷν ἀναπείθει, λέγων· «Ἐὰν δὲ μὴ ἰσχύῃ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ τὸ ἱκανὸν εἰς τὸ πρόβατον, οἴσει περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας αὐτοῦ, ἧς ἥμαρτε, δύο τρυγόνας, ἢ δύο νοσσοὺς περιστερῶν Κυρίῳ, ἕνα περὶ ἁμαρτίας, καὶ ἕνα εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα, καὶ οἴσει αὐτὰ πρὸς τὸν ἱερέα, καὶ προσάξει ὁ ἱερεὺς τὸ περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας πρότερον, καὶ ἀποκνίσει ὁ ἱερεὺς τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τοῦ σφονδύλου, καὶ οὐ διελεῖ, καὶ ῥανεῖ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος τοῦ περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ἐπὶ τὸν τοῖχον τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου. Τὸ δὲ κατάλοιπον τοῦ αἵματος καταστραγγιεῖ ἐπὶ τὴν βάσιν τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου. Ἁμαρτίας γάρ ἐστι, καὶ τὸ δεύτερον ποιήσει ὁλοκαύτωμα ὡς καθήκει· καὶ ἐξιλάσεται περὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ ἱερεὺς περὶ τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ἧς ἥμαρτε, καὶ ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ.» Τρυγόνι μὲν δὴ καὶ περιστερᾷ παρεικαστέον εὖ μάλα τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν τὸν Χριστὸν, ὅτι τὸ μέν ἐστιν εὐφωνότατόν τε καὶ λαλίστατον ἐν στρουθίοις, τὸ δὲ ὅτι μάλιστα πρὸς ἄκρον ἥκει πραότητος. Ἄμφω δὲ ἦν ἐν Χριστῷ. Πᾶσαν μὲν γὰρ κατεκήλησε τὴν οἰκουμένην τοῖς εὐαγγελικοῖς κηρύγμασι, τρυγὼν ἡ ἄνωθέν τε καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, λιγυρὸν ὥσπερ ἐνιεῖσα μέλος, καὶ τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρὸς κατατρανοῦσα θέλησιν. Ὡς γὰρ ὁ θεσπέσιος Ἰωάννης φησὶν, «Ὃν ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Θεὸς, τὰ ῥήματα τοῦ Θεοῦ λαλεῖ.» Ἐκάλει δὲ καὶ ἡμᾶς πρὸς μίμησιν τῆς ἐνούσης αὐτῷ πραότητός τε καὶ ἡμερότητος, οὕτω λέγων· «Ἄρατε τὸν ζυγόν μου
pass_a_gloss: [Leviticus 5:6 continued from §11: ...for the sin which he sinned, a female from the sheep, a ewe lamb or a she-goat from the goats, for sin, and the priest will make atonement (ἐξιλάσκομαι) for him concerning his sin which he sinned, and the sin will be forgiven him.] Observe, then, that the one who hears the voice of adjuration and makes the matter of no account at all, and the one liable to other defilements, and indeed besides this the one condemned for perjury (ψευδορκία), he sets in an equal and unvarying kind of offence. For contempt (καταφρόνησις) toward God is truly an extraordinary defilement, and leaps up to the very last of evils, and the offence is near and brother to the fleshly uncleannesses; or must one not set in equal account the accursed perjury and the contempt of adjuration? PALLADIUS: Very much so; for the charges are somehow always evenly matched on both. CYRIL: So release will follow for these also through confession (ἐξαγόρευσις), and indeed through the slaughter of a ewe lamb, that is, a sheep. [Isaiah 43:26 quoted: for you, say your lawless deeds first, that you may be justified.] And indeed the divine David also cries out: [Psalm 31:5 LXX quoted: I said, I will confess against myself my lawlessness to the Lord, and you forgave the impiety of my heart.] However, confessing alone does not suffice for the complete washing off (ἀπόνιψις), but the death of Christ frees entirely, he having suffered for us, and having put himself under the sins of all of us as in every form of the tame animals: in a calf, I mean, and indeed also in a sheep and a goat. And the law, as if making slackness (ῥᾳθυμία) about sacrifice without excuse for those in defilements and uncleannesses, if someone does not have a calf and a sheep, persuades him to honour with the things at hand and within his strength, saying: [Leviticus 5:7-10 quoted: if his hand is not strong enough for the sheep, he will bring for his sin which he sinned two turtledoves or two young of pigeons to the Lord, one for sin and one for whole burnt offering, and he will bring them to the priest, and the priest will bring the one for sin first, and the priest will nip off (ἀποκνίζω) its head from the neck bone, and will not divide it, and will sprinkle from the blood of the sin offering on the wall of the altar. And the rest of the blood he will drain out on the base of the altar. For it is a sin offering; and the second he will make a whole burnt offering as is fitting; and the priest will make atonement for him concerning the sin which he sinned, and it will be forgiven him.] To a turtledove (τρυγών) and a pigeon one must liken very well our Lord Jesus the Christ, because the one is most sweet-voiced and most talkative among birds, and the other comes as near as possible to the height of meekness. And both were in Christ. For he charmed (κατακηλέω) the whole inhabited world with the gospel preachings, the turtledove from above and from heaven, sending forth as it were a clear-toned song, and making plain the will of God the Father. For as the inspired John says: [John 3:34 quoted: he whom God sent speaks the words of God.] And he also called us to imitation of the meekness and tameness that were in him, saying thus: [Matthew 11:29 begun: take my yoke...] [continues in §13]
pass_a_gloss_with_greek: [Lev 5:6 continued from §11:] (ἁμαρ)τίας ἧς ἥμαρτε, θῆλυ ἀπὸ τῶν προβάτων, ἀμνάδα (ewe lamb) ἢ χίμαιραν (she-goat) ἐξ αἰγῶν περὶ ἁμαρτίας; ἐξιλάσεται (make atonement) ὁ ἱερεύς; ἀφεθήσεται αὐτῷ ἡ ἁμαρτία. Ἄθρει 'observe' ὅτι τὸν ὁρκισμοῦ φωνῆς ἐπαΐοντα 'the one hearing the voice of adjuration' καὶ παρ' οὐδὲν τὸ πρᾶγμα πεποιημένον 'having made the matter of no account', καὶ τὸν ἑτέροις ἔνοχον μολυσμοῖς 'liable to other defilements', καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ τὸν ἐπὶ τῇ ψευδορκίᾳ κατεγνωσμένον 'condemned for perjury', ἐν ἴσῳ τε καὶ ἀπαραλλάκτῳ τίθησι πλημμελείας τρόπῳ 'sets in an equal and unvarying mode of offence'. μολυσμὸς ἐξαίσιος 'extraordinary defilement' ... εἰς τὸ λοῖσθον ἀναθρώσκει τῶν κακῶν 'leaps up to the last/extreme of evils', ἡ εἰς Θεὸν καταφρόνησις 'contempt toward God'; καὶ ταῖς σαρκικαῖς ἀκαθαρσίαις ἐγγὺς καὶ ἀδελφὸν τὸ πλημμέλημα 'near and sibling to fleshly uncleannesses the offence'. ἢ οὐκ ἐν ἴσῳ θετέον λόγῳ τὴν ἐπάρατον (accursed) ψευδορκίαν καὶ ὁρκισμοῦ καταφρόνησιν; ΠΑΛΛ.: Πάνυ μὲν οὖν· ἰσοπαλῆ (evenly matched) ἐπ' ἀμφοῖν ἀεὶ τὰ ἐγκλήματα. ΚΥΡ.: Ἕψεται (ἕπομαι) καὶ τούτοις ἡ λύσις 'release' δι' ἐξαγορεύσεως 'through confession' καὶ ἀμνάδος, ἤτοι προβάτου σφαγῆς 'slaughter of a ewe lamb, i.e. a sheep'. Isa 43:26 LXX: Λέγε σὺ τὰς ἀνομίας σου πρῶτος, ἵνα δικαιωθῇς. ὁ θεῖος Δαβίδ ἀναφωνεῖ, Ps 31:5 LXX: Εἶπα· Ἐξαγορεύσω κατ' ἐμοῦ τὴν ἀνομίαν μου τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ σὺ ἀφῆκας τὴν ἀσέβειαν τῆς καρδίας μου. Πλὴν οὐκ ἀπόχρη εἰς τὴν τελείαν ἀπόνιψιν 'complete washing-off' τὸ ἐξαγορεῦσαι μόνον; ἀπαλλάττει παντελῶς 'frees entirely' ὁ Χριστοῦ θάνατος, παθόντος ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν, καὶ ταῖς ἁπάντων ἡμῶν ἁμαρτίαις ἑαυτὸν ὑποφέροντος 'submitting himself under the sins of us all' ὡς ἐν εἴδει παντὶ τῶν ἡμέρων ζώων 'as in every form of the tame animals': μόσχῳ, προβάτῳ, αἰγί. Ἀπροφάσιστον (without excuse) καθιστὰς ὁ νόμος τὸ ῥᾴθυμον (slackness) εἰς θυσίαν τοῖς ἐν μολυσμοῖς καὶ ἀκαθαρσίαις, εἰ μὴ μόσχον ἔχοι καὶ πρόβατον, τοῖς κατὰ χεῖρα καὶ ἐν ἰσχύϊ τιμᾶν ἀναπείθει 'persuades (him) to honour with things at hand and within strength'. Quote Lev 5:7–10 LXX: ἐὰν μὴ ἰσχύῃ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ τὸ ἱκανὸν εἰς τὸ πρόβατον, οἴσει ... δύο τρυγόνας ἢ δύο νοσσοὺς περιστερῶν, ἕνα περὶ ἁμαρτίας, ἕνα εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα; προσάξει τὸ περὶ ἁμαρτίας πρότερον; ἀποκνίσει (nip off) τὴν κεφαλὴν ἀπὸ τοῦ σφονδύλου (neck vertebra) καὶ οὐ διελεῖ (not divide); ῥανεῖ (sprinkle) ... ἐπὶ τὸν τοῖχον τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου; κατάλοιπον τοῦ αἵματος καταστραγγιεῖ (drain out) ἐπὶ τὴν βάσιν; ἁμαρτίας γάρ ἐστι; τὸ δεύτερον ποιήσει ὁλοκαύτωμα ὡς καθήκει; ἐξιλάσεται ... ἀφεθήσεται. Τρυγόνι καὶ περιστερᾷ παρεικαστέον (to be compared) τὸν Κύριον ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν τὸν Χριστόν: τὸ μὲν εὐφωνότατον καὶ λαλίστατον ἐν στρουθίοις 'most sweet-voiced and most talkative among birds', τὸ δὲ ὅτι μάλιστα πρὸς ἄκρον ἥκει πραότητος 'comes most nearly to the height of meekness'. Ἄμφω ἦν ἐν Χριστῷ. κατεκήλησε (κατακηλέω 'charm, enchant') τὴν οἰκουμένην τοῖς εὐαγγελικοῖς κηρύγμασι, τρυγὼν ἡ ἄνωθέν τε καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, λιγυρὸν (clear-toned) ἐνιεῖσα μέλος 'sending forth a song', τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρὸς κατατρανοῦσα (make clear) θέλησιν. ὁ θεσπέσιος Ἰωάννης: Ὃν ἀπέστειλεν ὁ Θεὸς, τὰ ῥήματα τοῦ Θεοῦ λαλεῖ (John 3:34). Ἐκάλει ἡμᾶς πρὸς μίμησιν τῆς ἐνούσης αὐτῷ πραότητός τε καὶ ἡμερότητος, saying: Ἄρατε τὸν ζυγόν μου [continues in §13].
pass_b_english: Cyril: …he committed, a female from the flock, a ewe lamb or a she-goat from the goats, for sin; and the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he committed, and the sin shall be forgiven him’ (Leviticus 5:6). Observe, then, that the law sets in one equal and identical class of offense the man who hears the voice of adjuration and makes nothing at all of the matter, the man liable for other defilements, and, besides these, the man condemned for perjury. For contempt toward God is truly a monstrous defilement, and it rises to the very extreme of evil; and this offense is near and akin to the uncleannesses of the flesh. Or must we not count accursed perjury and contempt for adjuration as equal?
Palladius: Certainly; for in both cases the charges are always, in a way, evenly matched.

Cyril: Then for these also release will follow through confession and through the slaying of a ewe lamb, that is, a sheep. For, it says, ‘Be the first to tell your lawless deeds, that you may be justified’ (Isaiah 43:26). And the divine David also cries out: ‘I said, I will confess my lawlessness against myself to the Lord; and you forgave the ungodliness of my heart’ (Psalm 32:5). Yet confession alone is not enough to wash us completely clean. It is the death of Christ that sets us entirely free, for he suffered for us and put himself under the sins of us all, as in every kind of domestic animal: I mean in the calf, and in the sheep and the goat. And the law, as if to leave those in defilements and uncleannesses no excuse for neglecting sacrifice, urges anyone who has no calf or sheep to give honor with what is at hand and within his means, saying: ‘If his hand is not strong enough to provide a sheep, he shall bring to the Lord for the sin he committed two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. And he shall bring them to the priest, and the priest shall offer the one for sin first; and the priest shall pinch off its head from the neck, and shall not divide it. And he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the wall of the altar, and the rest of the blood he shall drain out at the base of the altar; for it is a sin offering. And the second he shall make a whole burnt offering, as is fitting; and the priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he committed, and it shall be forgiven him’ (Leviticus 5:7–10). We should compare our Lord Jesus Christ, and very fittingly, to the turtledove and the dove, because the one has the sweetest voice and is the most vocal of birds, and the other comes nearest to the height of meekness. Both were in Christ. For he, the turtledove from above and from heaven, charmed the whole world with the preaching of the Gospel, sending forth, as it were, a clear and sweet song, and making plain the will of God the Father. For as the inspired John says: ‘He whom God has sent speaks the words of God’ (John 3:34). And he also called us to imitate the meekness and gentleness that were in him, saying: ‘Take my yoke… (Matthew 11:29)

choices.why: Lev 5:6/5:7/5:10 'the sin that he sinned' -> 'the sin he committed' (natural English, same sense); opening now joins §11 '…for the sin… …he committed'

choices.english: sets in one equal and identical class of offence
rejected: puts on one and the same footing of offence
choices.why: 'puts on one and the same footing of offence' -> 'sets in one equal and identical class of offence' (ἐν ἴσῳ τε καὶ ἀπαραλλάκτῳ); 'guilty of' -> 'liable for' (ἔνοχον); 'convicted' -> 'condemned' (κατεγνωσμένον)
'voice of an oath' / 'contempt for an oath' -> 'adjuration', matching Lev 5:1

choices.english: rises to the very extreme of evil
rejected: leaps up to the very extreme of evils
choices.why: 'leaps up to the very extreme of evils' -> 'rises to the very extreme of evil'

choices.english: Be the first to tell your lawless deeds
rejected: For you, tell your lawless deeds first
choices.why: Isaiah 43:26: 'For you, tell your lawless deeds first' -> 'Be the first to tell your lawless deeds' (λέγε σὺ … πρῶτος); γάρ moved to Cyril's frame
'for complete washing' -> 'to wash us completely clean'

choices.english: put himself under the sins of us all
rejected: submitted himself to the sins of us all
choices.why: 'submitted himself to the sins of us all' -> 'put himself under the sins of us all' (old wording could read as submitting to sin); 'tame animal' -> 'domestic animal'

choices.english: to leave … no excuse for neglecting sacrifice
rejected: leaving slackness about sacrifice without excuse
choices.why: 'leaving slackness about sacrifice without excuse' -> 'to leave … no excuse for neglecting sacrifice'; 'pay his honour … reach and strength' -> 'give honour with what is at hand and within his means'

apparatus.note: PG OCR; a column may cut mid-sentence or mid-word.

changes: Lev 5:6/5:7/5:10 'the sin that he sinned' -> 'the sin he committed' (natural English, same sense); opening now joins §11 '…for the sin… …he committed'

'puts on one and the same footing of offence' -> 'sets in one equal and identical class of offence' (ἐν ἴσῳ τε καὶ ἀπαραλλάκτῳ); 'guilty of' -> 'liable for' (ἔνοχον); 'convicted' -> 'condemned' (κατεγνωσμένον)
'voice of an oath' / 'contempt for an oath' -> 'adjuration', matching Lev 5:1
'leaps up to the very extreme of evils' -> 'rises to the very extreme of evil'
Isaiah 43:26: 'For you, tell your lawless deeds first' -> 'Be the first to tell your lawless deeds' (λέγε σὺ … πρῶτος); γάρ moved to Cyril's frame
'for complete washing' -> 'to wash us completely clean'
'submitted himself to the sins of us all' -> 'put himself under the sins of us all' (old wording could read as submitting to sin); 'tame animal' -> 'domestic animal'
'leaving slackness about sacrifice without excuse' -> 'to leave … no excuse for neglecting sacrifice'; 'pay his honour … reach and strength' -> 'give honour with what is at hand and within his means'
παρεικαστέον: 'We may … compare' -> 'We should compare' (verbal adjective = obligation, not permission)
'most talkative of birds' -> 'most vocal of birds'; 'gentleness' -> 'meekness' for πραότης (consistent with §11)
Turtledove sentence reordered so the subject 'he, the turtledove from above' stands first
Matthew 11:29 citation moved beside the quoted clause
Checked: Leviticus 5:6, Isaiah 43:26 LXX, Psalm 31:5 LXX = Psalm 32:5, Leviticus 5:7–10, John 3:34, Matthew 11:29 all correct
